title: Adaptive Renewal Buffer and Graduated Expansion Path
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers report a mismatch between committed annual spends and observed consumption patterns. Existing true-up rules are either too punitive (large one-time charges at renewal) or too loose (under-indexed against growth), which causes renewal friction and lost expansion opportunities. We need a pricing mechanism that smooths renewal true-ups, preserves revenue predictability, and creates clear expansion incentives for customers.

Proposal (high level): Introduce an Adaptive Renewal Buffer (ARB) combined with a Graduated Expansion Path (GEP). ARB provides a small built-in credit/buffer tied to percent-growth over the preceding 12 months, reducing surprise overage charges at renewal. GEP defines clear multi-year uplift bands and credits that scale with usage growth, making it easier for customers to commit to multi-year commitments while preserving economics for Redwood.

Key mechanics: 1) ARB = min(10% of committed ARR, floor of 5k USD) that automatically cushions up to X% of a customer's year-over-year usage increase when calculating renewal true-ups. 2) GEP defines three uplift bands for multi-year renewals: modest growth (0-25% YoY) -> 0-5% price uplift, expanding growth (25-75% YoY) -> 6-18% uplift with staged invoice tranches, and hyper-growth (>75% YoY) -> bespoke uplift + expansion commit conversation. 3) True-up smoothing: divide any true-up amount above ARB across next N billing periods (N = contract length in quarters, capped at 8) to avoid large one-time invoices. 4) Offer a ‘grace allocation’ for first-year expansions when customers sign a multi-year commit within renewal window (e.g., additional 5% free allocation for 12 months) to encourage early expansion commitments.

Goals and success metrics: 1) Reduce renewal churn attributable to invoice surprise by 30% within two quarters. 2) Increase multi-year renewal rate among midmarket and growth accounts by 12% year-over-year. 3) Preserve or improve ARR retention (net revenue retention >= 105% among participating cohorts). 4) Keep short-term cash collection impact to <2% ARR deferral vs current baseline.

Segmentation and eligibility: Start with a pilot cohort of 60 accounts (mix of midmarket and growth enterprise customers, $150k to $2M ARR). Exclude accounts on dedicated private contracts with special pricing. Rollout contingent on legal and finance sign-off and updated contract language.

Pricing experiments to run: A) Control (status quo true-up). B) ARB only (buffer + same uplift bands). C) ARB + GEP with smoothing. D) ARB + GEP + grace allocation. Randomize cohorts controlling for ARR band and renewal month.

Financial modeling assumptions: churn elasticity of -0.8 per 1% increase in invoice surprise; average historical YoY growth for pilot cohort 22%; expected uplift revenue capture incremental 4-8% ARR for cohorts B/C. Modeled cashflow impact included in attachment.

Stakeholders: PM (Ava Martinez), Finance (Leo Patel), Legal (Marina Gupta), Sales Ops (Jordan Park), Customer Success (Nina Alvarez), Revenue Strategy (Hiro Tanaka), Engineering for billing automation (Riley Chen).

Risks and mitigation: 1) Perceived complexity by sales — mitigate with a one-page cheat sheet and automation in quoting tools. 2) Revenue timing risk — model and cap smoothing windows, require GAAP accounting alignment with finance. 3) Contract/legal pushback on new language — run parallel opt-in pilot with standard amendment language and collect feedback.

Rollout plan: 1) Finish proposal + modeling (this ticket). 2) Create contract amendment templates and QRG for Sales. 3) Build billing automation and reporting for smoothing and ARB application (Engineering ticket ENG-49211). 4) Pilot 60 customers over 3 renewal cohorts (6 months). 5) Analyze and iterate; expand to broader eligible population if NRR goals met.

Deliverables: PRD, finance model, legal amendment, sales playbook, pilot cohort tracker, CS playbook for customer conversations.

Confluence/Artifacts: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRG/pages/ARB-GEP-2026 (primary PRD), https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/arb-models, GitHub billing automation epic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/epics/ARB-GEP
